nodes.name: 參木 (Sanki)
nodes.occupation: Bank employee (銀行員), later employee at Tōyō Spinning Co. (東洋紡絲會社) in the trading department (取引部).
nodes.summary: A thoughtful, disillusioned man working in Shanghai. He contemplates suicide but is held back by thoughts of his mother and his secret love for Kyōko. He is critical of his superiors and societal hypocrisy, gets fired from his bank job, finds new work through Takashige, and becomes entangled with several women (O-Sugi, Olga, Hō Shūran, Miyako) while navigating the city's turmoil and his own internal conflicts.

nodes.name: 甲谷 (Kōya)
nodes.occupation: Works for a lumber company (材木會社) in Singapore, acting as a foreign relations officer (外交部).
nodes.age: Not specified, but Sanki's childhood friend.
nodes.summary: Sanki's ambitious and somewhat opportunistic childhood friend from Singapore. He comes to Shanghai seeking a wife and business opportunities, becomes infatuated with Miyako, and interacts callously with O-Sugi. He engages in political and economic discussions but is primarily driven by personal gain and desire.

nodes.name: 宮子 (Miyako)
nodes.aliases: Miss Miyako (ミス・宮子), Miyako-jō (宮子嬢)
nodes.occupation: Dancer / Dance hall girl (踊子 / ダンスガール).
nodes.summary: A popular and sought-after dancer who enjoys the attention of numerous foreign men. She is sharp-witted, independent, and plays hard-to-get with Kōya, eventually rejecting him. She later develops a complex, provocative relationship with Sanki.

nodes.name: 競子 (Kyōko)
nodes.summary: Kōya's younger sister, whom Sanki deeply loves. She is married to a man dying of tuberculosis. Her potential widowhood gives Sanki conflicted hope.

nodes.name: お柳 (O-Ryu)
nodes.occupation: Runs a Turkish bath (浴場の店主), mistress (妾) of Qian Shishan.
nodes.summary: The calculating and sensual proprietress of a Turkish bath and mistress to a wealthy Chinese man. She has a prominent spider tattoo, manipulates situations for her own benefit, dismisses O-Sugi cruelly, and interacts flirtatiously but transactionally with Kōya.

nodes.name: お杉 (O-Sugi)
nodes.occupation: Bath attendant (湯女), later prostitute (春婦).
nodes.summary: A quiet bath attendant initially liked by Sanki. She is victimized by O-Ryu and Kōya, loses her job, and tragically turns to prostitution. She remains uncertain about who assaulted her and retains feelings for Sanki.

nodes.name: 山口 (Yamaguchi)
nodes.occupation: Architect (建築師), later "corpse collector" / skeleton dealer (死人拾ひ).
nodes.summary: An old acquaintance of Kōya and Sanki, an architect turned morbid businessman dealing in human skeletons. He identifies as an "Asia-ist," keeps multiple mistresses (including Olga), and offers Sanki a job in his skeleton business. He has a cynical yet sometimes friendly relationship with the main characters.

nodes.name: オルガ (Oruga / Olga)
nodes.summary: A Russian refugee, formerly an aristocrat(?), kept as a mistress first by Kimura, then Yamaguchi. She suffers from epilepsy, feels lonely and displaced, develops feelings for Sanki, and recounts her family's traumatic escape from the Russian Revolution.

nodes.name: 高重 (Takashige)
nodes.occupation: Works supervisor (工人係り) at Tōyō Spinning Co. (東洋紡績).
nodes.summary: Kōya's pragmatic and cynical older brother. He manages workers at a Japanese-owned mill, is aware Hō Shūran is a communist operative among his workers, and is deeply concerned about strikes and political unrest affecting his factory and Japanese interests. He helps Sanki find a job.

nodes.name: 芳秋蘭 (Hō Shūran)
nodes.age: Not specified, appears young and elegant.
nodes.summary: An elegant and beautiful Chinese woman who is a dedicated communist activist working undercover in Takashige's factory. She attracts Kōya's attention and later develops a complex relationship with Sanki after he rescues her during a riot, engaging him in ideological debates. She is a key figure in the strikes and unrest. Rumored to be assassinated later.

Kōya flees towards them, and they deter his pursuers.

Initially uninterested, later seeks Sanki out, recognizing a kindred spirit in his disillusionment. She engages him in provocative conversations, challenges his relationship with Kyōko and his ideals, expresses vulnerability mixed with manipulation, and initiates physical intimacy. She seems drawn to his complexity and sadness.

Kōya is infatuated and pursues her relentlessly for marriage. Miyako enjoys his attention and gifts but finds him somewhat naive and ultimately rejects his proposal, preferring her independence and the excitement of Shanghai.
Yamaguchi observes Miyako at the dance hall and warns Kōya about her manipulative nature, suggesting she might be a spy. He notes her preference for foreigners.
Miyako points out Shūran to Kōya at the dance hall. Later implies Shūran might be a better match for Sanki, possibly indicating awareness or rivalry.
Miyako fondly recalls dancing with Michel, a French technician, for 13 days. He is one of her five main lovers whose gifts she keeps.
One of Miyako's main lovers, a German businessman (AEG manager). She arranges to meet him, using it to dismiss Kōya. He competes for her attention with Kleber.
One of Miyako's main lovers, an American businessman (GE employee). He competes for her attention with Filzel, engaging in business rivalry banter over her.
One of Miyako's foreign admirers/lovers whom she mentions needing to meet.

Miyako is the center of attention for numerous foreign men at the dance hall, skillfully managing their advances and rivalries.

Identified by Yamaguchi as competing for Miyako's attention. Kleber (#18) is one.
Mentioned by Miyako as one of the men competing for her attention, trying to find her "weak spot."

Miyako tells Sanki about seeing a Japanese man attacked near her residence.
Miyako tells Sanki about seeing an injured Japanese person being transported by car.
Miyako receives bread from a British volunteer during the shortages, which she later offers to Sanki.

Sanki is deeply in love with Kyōko. Thoughts of her are central to his emotional life and his struggle against despair. Her glance as she left once reminded him of the departing prostitute (#5). He clings to the hope of being with her if her husband dies.
Kōya is her older brother. He learns of Sanki's feelings for her belatedly and discusses her situation (husband's illness, potential return) with Sanki and Takashige.
Takashige is her older brother, who discusses her situation with Kōya and Sanki.
She is married to him. His impending death from tuberculosis creates the central romantic conflict for Sanki.

O-Ryu is attracted to Sanki but he consistently rejects her advances. She becomes jealous when he shows interest (real or feigned) in O-Sugi, leading her to cruelly dismiss O-Sugi. Sanki views her as manipulative.

O-Ryu engages in sensual and often combative banter with Kōya. She uses her position to control situations, offers information (about O-Sugi, Hō Shūran), and facilitates Kōya's meeting with her patron, Qian Shishan. Their relationship is physical and opportunistic.
O-Ryu is O-Sugi's employer. Jealous of Sanki's perceived interest in O-Sugi, she violently abuses and fires O-Sugi, directly causing her descent into prostitution.
O-Ryu knows Shūran meets secretly with Qian Shishan. She refers to Shūran as a rival for Qian's money, not affection. She agrees to help Kōya spy on Shūran.
O-Ryu is the proprietress employing the bath attendants.
The attendant who announces Qian Shishan's arrival to O-Ryu and Kōya.
Seen laughing with O-Ryu when Kōya enters Qian Shishan's room.

O-Sugi initially admires Sanki from afar. She becomes a pawn in his interaction with O-Ryu, leading to her abuse and dismissal. She seeks refuge at his place, is ambiguously assaulted, and leaves when he doesn't return. She retains feelings for him, eventually taking him in when he is destitute, leading to intimacy despite her changed circumstances and shame.
Kōya finds O-Sugi at Sanki's place and assaults her. He later dismisses her as insignificant. O-Sugi remains unsure if he or Sanki was her assailant. She observes him later with O-Ryu at the market.
O-Sugi works for O-Ryu, who becomes jealous and cruelly dismisses her after Sanki's intervention. O-Ryu informs Kōya of O-Sugi's new profession.

Yamaguchi develops an interest in O-Sugi, finding her innocent appeal contrasting with other women. He is dismayed to hear she's been fired and asks Shizue to find her. He later intends to visit her where she works as a prostitute.
Shizue informs Yamaguchi that O-Sugi has been fired and expresses sympathy.
O-Sugi considers emulating Tatsue, who is seemingly a prostitute, as a means of survival after losing her job.
He laughs at her after she leaves the bathhouse; she runs away.
Follows her briefly after the coolie incident; she tells him off and flees.
O-Sugi propositions him after deciding to become a prostitute.
O-Sugi remembers her mother who committed suicide due to a pension dispute.
O-Sugi remembers her deceased father, an army colonel.
The men who pay for O-Sugi's services after she becomes a prostitute.
O-Sugi considers finding a kind customer to help her return to Japan.
A picture of him is on O-Sugi's wall.
A former client who left belongings in O-Sugi's room.

Yamaguchi offers Sanki a job managing his skeleton business, gives him Olga to look after, and engages in political debates. He seems amused by Sanki's existential angst but also shows some friendly concern.

They reminisce, discuss Sanki, women, business, and politics. Yamaguchi provides cynical commentary and information. Kōya later seeks refuge at Yamaguchi's house, leading to further strange interactions involving the skeleton business and Olga.
Yamaguchi observes Miyako and warns Kōya about her, suggesting she is manipulative and possibly a spy.
Yamaguchi becomes interested in O-Sugi's perceived innocence. He is concerned when she is fired and later intends to visit her as a prostitute.
Yamaguchi keeps Olga as a mistress after Kimura discards her. He tasks Sanki with looking after her, aware of her loneliness and epilepsy, and seems possessive when Sanki tries to leave her.
Yamaguchi interacts with Takashige, discussing Kōya, Hō Shūran, and the political situation. He knows Takashige from before.

Yamaguchi knows of Shūran through his "Asia-ist" connections and points her out to Kōya. He mentions her association with Takashige. Later hears rumors of her death and morbidly considers acquiring her skeleton.
Yamaguchi mentions Furuya is buying geisha wives on installment.
Yamaguchi mentions Mihashi is not taking care of himself.
Yamaguchi recounts Kimura's gambling addiction and cruel treatment of mistresses, calling him a madman. Olga was previously Kimura's mistress.
Shizue informs Yamaguchi about O-Sugi being fired; he pays her for potential future information.
Fellow "Asia-ist". They discuss the volatile political situation, Indian nationalism, communism, and the strike's implications. Yamaguchi buys a ring from Amuri.
Yamaguchi mentions past arguments with Li within the Asia-ist circle and gives Kōya a letter from Li.
The man working in Yamaguchi's basement cleaning bones.
Yamaguchi uses them (implicitly) in his skeleton preparation.
Yamaguchi uses a large number of rats to help clean skeletons in his basement, claiming they "cleanse the earth."

Entrusted to Sanki's care by Yamaguchi. She develops strong feelings for Sanki, clings to him out of loneliness and fear, pleads with him to stay and take her to Japan. Her advances are met with his detachment, leading to emotional outbursts and physical struggles. She suffers an epileptic seizure while recounting her past to Kōya, mentioning Sanki fondly.
After Yamaguchi leaves, Olga confides in Kōya about her past, her epilepsy, and her feelings for Sanki. She has a seizure while talking to him; he cares for her, leading to intimacy.
Yamaguchi keeps Olga as a mistress. He is aware of her epilepsy and loneliness, using Sanki as a temporary caretaker. He shows some possessiveness but also transactional detachment.
Olga was bought and kept as a mistress by Kimura, who treated her cruelly and eventually sold her to Yamaguchi after gambling losses.
Escaped Russia with Olga and her father. Cleverly saved her husband from execution in Tomsk by fabricating a story.
Escaped Russia with Olga and her mother. Narrowly avoided execution in Tomsk. Later died in Harbin while trading jewels. Olga remembers him holding her during seizures.
The revolutionary tribunal chairman in Tomsk who nearly executed Olga's father.
Olga observes the crowd at the revolutionary tribunal in Tomsk.

Takashige hires Sanki after he loses his bank job, placing him in a dangerous position at the factory during unrest. He engages Sanki in philosophical and political discussions, offering cynical advice. He is aware of Sanki's feelings for Kyōko.

Takashige is Kōya's older brother. They have contrasting personalities (pragmatic vs. opportunistic). Takashige expresses concern about Kōya's activities in Shanghai and they discuss family (Kyōko) and the political situation.
Kyōko is Takashige's younger sister. He discusses her husband's impending death and her potential return to Shanghai with Kōya and Sanki.
Takashige encounters Yamaguchi, discusses Kōya and Hō Shūran. Yamaguchi knows him from before.

Takashige knows Shūran is a communist working undercover in his factory. He chooses not to expose her, finding a cynical "enjoyment" in their covert conflict, but recognizes her influence and potential threat, predicting she might try to kill him or be killed herself.
Mentioned briefly as someone who shouldn't overhear his concerns about being killed.
Takashige manages the Chinese workers at the factory, dealing with their demands, potential strikes, and communist infiltration.
Takashige's window overlooks their encampment.
The general group of workers under his supervision during the night shift riot.
Takashige points her out to Sanki as an example of low wages.
Takashige notes that Shūran is collaborating with this faction.
The police assigned to the factory, fighting alongside Takashige during the riot.
The workers in the scutching room, noted as dangerous elements.
Takashige leads the defense against the rioters attacking the factory.

The workers initially defending the factory under Takashige, who later switch sides.
Takashige leads the Japanese staff during the riot, eventually ordering them to fire on the crowd.
The Japanese staff fighting alongside Takashige.
Arrives after Takashige and his men have repelled the rioters.
The faction within his factory guarding machinery against anti-communists during the shutdown.

Sanki is captivated by her beauty and rescues her during the factory riot. They have intense debates about communism, nationalism, and politics. She develops feelings, kissing him, but their fundamental differences lead to separation. She gives him a contact note before disappearing, rumored killed.
